title: Generation of hypoxia-sensing chimeric antigen receptor T cells
author: Kosti, Larios-Martinez, et al.
materials: T cells are counted and activated as shown.

This protocol describes how to purify T cells from the PBMC fraction using human pan T cell isolation kit (Miltenyi Biotec), a MidiMACs separator and LS columns (Miltenyi Biotec) and how to activate purified T cells using CD3/CD28 Human T-Activator Dynabeads (Gibco) (Figure 6).35.For T cell isolation:a.Count the cells from the PBMC fraction and proceed according to the manufacturers’ protocol: https://www.miltenyibiotec.com/US-en/products/pan-t-cell-isolation-kit-human.html#gref36.For T cell activation:b.Wash the CD3/CD28 Human T-Activator Dynabeads according to the manufacturers’ protocol: https://www.thermofisher.com/uk/en/home/references/protocols/proteins-expression-isolation-and-analysis/t-cell-activation-and-expansion/dynabeads-human-t-activator-cd3-cd28.htmlc.Resuspend the purified T cells at a concentration of 3 × 106 cells/mL in R5 media.d.Add Dynabeads Human T-Activator CD3/CD28 at a bead-to-cell ratio of 1:1.e.Seed 3 mL of the T cells containing the Dynabeads (3 × 106 cells/mL) per well on a TC-treated 6-well plate.f.Place plate into incubator.37.After 24 h add recombinant human IL-2 at a final concentration of 100 IU/mL.

steps.title: Prepare HEK293T cells for virus production
steps.instruction: Thaw a vial of HEK293T cells (~1×10⁷ cells in 1 mL) at 37 °C, seed in a T75 flask with 25 mL pre‑warmed I10 medium, incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ and monitor confluency over the next days.

steps.title: Seed HEK293T cells one day before transfection
steps.instruction: Prepare a suspension of HEK293T cells at 2.3×10⁵ cells/mL in I10, add 11 mL to a 100 mm plate (total 2.5×10⁶ cells), gently rock for even distribution and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Transfect HEK293T cells with retroviral plasmids
steps.instruction: For each 100 mm plate, mix 1.133 mL IMDM with 68 µL FuGENE in a 1.5 mL tube; in a second tube combine 5.6 µg RDF envelope plasmid, 8.5 µg Peq‑Pam‑env, and 8.5 µg vector plasmid (total volume <100 µL); incubate the combined mixtures at 20‑22 °C for 15 min, add dropwise to the cells, rock gently and return plate to the incubator.

steps.title: Replace medium 24 h post‑transfection
steps.instruction: At 24 h after transfection, discard the existing medium and add 11 mL pre‑warmed fresh I10 medium to each plate.

steps.title: Harvest first viral supernatant at 48 h
steps.instruction: At 48 h post‑transfection, collect the medium into a 50 mL Falcon tube, store at 4 °C, and replace with 11 mL warm fresh I10 medium.

steps.title: Harvest second viral supernatant and filter
steps.instruction: At 72 h post‑transfection, collect the medium into a 50 mL Falcon tube, store at 4 °C, filter the combined 48 h and 72 h supernatants through a 0.45 µm sterile filter (or centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min and collect supernatant), keep on ice or snap‑freeze; avoid storing at 4 °C for more than 1 day.

steps.title: Isolate PBMCs from donor blood
steps.instruction: Withdraw ~50 mL peripheral blood, transfer to 50 mL Falcon tubes, dilute 1:1 with RPMI, add 15 mL Ficoll‑Paque Plus to a new 50 mL tube, carefully layer 30 mL diluted blood over the Ficoll, centrifuge at 750 × g for 30 min at 20 °C (acceleration/brake = 0), collect the PBMC interface, optionally remove the plasma layer above it, add RPMI to a final volume of 50 mL, centrifuge 500 × g 5 min (acceleration/brake = 9), discard supernatant, repeat wash if multiple tubes, centrifuge again 500 × g 5 min, discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL R5 media.

steps.title: Isolate pan T cells using magnetic kit
steps.instruction: Count PBMCs and perform the human pan T‑cell isolation kit protocol (Miltenyi) using a MidiMACS separator and LS columns according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Activate T cells with CD3/CD28 Dynabeads
steps.instruction: Wash CD3/CD28 Human T‑Activator Dynabeads per manufacturer, resuspend purified T cells at 3×10⁶ cells/mL in R5, add beads at a 1:1 bead‑to‑cell ratio, seed 3 mL (3×10⁶ cells) per well of a TC‑treated 6‑well plate, incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, and after 24 h add recombinant human IL‑2 to a final concentration of 100 IU/mL.

steps.title: Prepare T cells for hypoxia assay
steps.instruction: Harvest transduced and non‑transduced T cells (maintain ~1×10⁶ cells/mL), collect at least 2.5 mL per culture into 15 mL Falcon tubes, centrifuge 500 × g 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend in 1 mL R5, count and adjust to 1×10⁶ cells/mL, dispense 1 mL into each well of two 24‑well plates (one for normoxia, one for hypoxia) for each construct.

steps.title: Set up hypoxic chamber gas flow
steps.instruction: Place the hypoxia plate on the polycarbonate tray inside the chamber, add a 20 mm Petri dish with 10–20 mL sterile water, close lid and ring clamp, open inlet and outlet clamps, connect the flow meter to the inlet, open the gas cylinder, set regulator to 8–10 psi, adjust flow to 25 L/min, purge the chamber for 4 min, then close the gas cylinder valve, clamp inlet and outlet, disconnect tubing, turn off the valve, and place the chamber in the incubator alongside the normoxic plate.

steps.title: Incubate cells under hypoxia and normoxia
steps.instruction: After the initial purge, incubate for 1 h, then repeat the purge steps (open clamps, purge 4 min at 25 L/min, close clamps) and continue incubation for an additional ≥17 h (total hypoxic exposure ≥18 h) while the normoxic plate remains in the incubator.

steps.title: Harvest cells for flow cytometry staining
steps.instruction: Remove the chamber from the incubator, open the outlet clamp (listen for a puff), open the chamber lid, withdraw 200 µL cell suspension from each condition, transfer to a 96‑well plate or Eppendorf tube, centrifuge 500 × g 5 min, discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 200 µL FACS buffer (PBS + 1 % FBS + 0.1 % sodium azide).

steps.title: Stain and analyze CAR expression by flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Perform the standard antibody staining protocol for CAR detection and analyze the samples on a flow cytometer according to usual laboratory practice.

description:
Note: This protocol describes the steps taken to express a generic chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) under a ‘dual oxygen-sensing’ expression system termed ‘HypoxiCAR’ using a Moloney murine leukemia (MoMLV) retroviral vector, SFG, as a means to achieve selective CAR and/or transgene expression in the tumor microenvironment when transduced into T cells. Although the approach can be expected to be applicable to other transgene carrier vectors (for example lentiviral vectors) and immune cell types, these have not been directly explored or optimized.
Note: Experimental results of the ‘single’ and ‘dual’ oxygen-sensing system used with a CAR, which are presented in this protocol, refer to a pan-ErbB-specific CAR designated T1E28z. T1E28z is a CD28-containing second generation CAR with specificity for eight distinct ErbB dimers found in many cancer types (Davies et al., 2012). Target recognition is achieved using the T1E peptide, which is a pan-ErbB ligand derived from transforming growth factor-α and epidermal growth factor (Stortelers et al., 2002). Selective expansion of retrovirus-engineered T1E28z+ T cells is achieved by co-expression of the CAR with the 4αβ receptor in a bicistronic single cassette separated from the CAR by a T2A sequence. 4αβ is a chimeric cytokine receptor in which the ectodomain of the IL-4 receptor α subunit has been fused to the transmembrane and endodomain of the shared IL-2/15 receptor β chain (Wilkie et al., 2010). Addition of IL-4 to T cells that co-express T1E28z and 4αβ (combination dubbed ‘T4’) permits the selective enrichment of only the gene-modified cells (Wilkie et al., 2010).
Note: Oxygen-sensing, as described here, relies on Hypoxia inducible factor (HIF)1α stabilization in the cell of interest when placed under limiting oxygen concentrations (typically <5% O2).
